request: if I flip two coins, what's the chance of exactly one head?

beats.intent: A tree: start splitting into H and T, each splitting again into H and T, four ends HH, HT, TH, TT
beats.narration: The first coin is heads or tails; for each, the second coin is heads or tails. Four equally likely outcomes.

beats.intent: The ends HT and TH lit green
beats.narration: Exactly one head happens two ways: heads then tails, or tails then heads.
Two out of four: a probability of one half.

request: can sticks of length 2, 3 and 6 make a triangle?

beats.intent: A base stick of 6 with sticks of 2 and 3 hinged at its ends, swinging up
beats.narration: Lay the six stick down and hinge the two and the three at its ends. Swing them up to try to meet.
beats.code:
stage.title("Can they make a triangle?")
k = 0.9
A, B = np.array([-3 * k, -1.5, 0]), np.array([3 * k, -1.5, 0])
base = Line(A, B, color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
s2 = Line(A, A + 2 * k * UP, color=BLUE, stroke_width=6)
s3 = Line(B, B + 3 * k * UP, color=ORANGE, stroke_width=6)
stage.play(Create(base), Create(s2), Create(s3))
stage.add(base, s2, s3)
stage.label(base, "6", direction=DOWN)
stage.label(s2, "2", direction=LEFT, color=BLUE)
stage.label(s3, "3", direction=RIGHT, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: Both sticks lowered flat along the base, still a gap of 1 between their tips
beats.narration: Even lying flat along the base they only reach two plus three, five. A gap of one is left: they can never meet.
beats.code:
stage.play(Rotate(s2, -PI / 2, about_point=A), Rotate(s3, PI / 2, about_point=B))
gap = Line(A + 2 * k * RIGHT, B - 3 * k * RIGHT, color=RED, stroke_width=10)
stage.play(Create(gap))
stage.add(gap)
stage.label(gap, "gap 1", direction=UP, color=RED)

beats.intent: The sticks beside 2 + 3 < 6, the triangle rule
beats.narration: Any two sides of a triangle must add up to more than the third. Two plus three is less than six, so no triangle.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"2 + 3 < 6")
stage.caption("two sides must add to more than the third")

beats.intent: A square cover being tilted over its square hole, its diagonal longer than the hole's side
beats.narration: A square cover can be turned on its edge and slipped down the diagonal of its hole: the diagonal is longer than the side.
beats.code:
stage.title("Why round covers?")
hole = Square(2.0, color=GREY_B).move_to([-3, -0.3, 0])
cover = Square(2.0, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.4).move_to([-3, -0.3, 0])
stage.play(Create(hole), FadeIn(cover))
stage.add(hole, cover)
diag = Line(hole.get_corner(DL), hole.get_corner(UR), color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(diag))
stage.add(diag)
stage.label(diag, "2.83", direction=UL, color=YELLOW)
stage.label(hole, "side 2", direction=DOWN)
edge = Line([-4.0, -0.3, 0], [-2.0, -0.3, 0], color=ORANGE, stroke_width=10)
stage.play(Transform(cover, edge))
stage.play(cover.animate.rotate(PI / 4))
stage.caption("on edge, it fits down the diagonal")

beats.intent: A round cover over its hole: every way across is the same width
beats.narration: A circle is the same width in every direction, so however you turn a round cover, it can't fit through its hole.
beats.code:
hole2 = Circle(radius=1.0, color=GREY_B).move_to([2.6, -0.3, 0])
cover2 = Circle(radius=1.1, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.4).move_to([2.6, -0.3, 0])
stage.play(Create(hole2), FadeIn(cover2))
stage.add(hole2, cover2)
for a in (0, PI / 4, PI / 2):
    d = Line(hole2.get_center() - 1.1 * np.array([np.cos(a), np.sin(a), 0]), hole2.get_center() + 1.1 * np.array([np.cos(a), np.sin(a), 0]), color=YELLOW)
    stage.play(Create(d), run_time=0.4)
    stage.add(d)
stage.caption("round: the same width every way")

request: how does a mirror reflect light?

beats.intent: A flat mirror with a ray coming in at an angle and the dashed normal line
beats.narration: A ray of light hits a flat mirror. Draw the normal: the line at right angles to the mirror where it hits.
beats.code:
stage.title("Angle in, angle out")
mirror = Line([-4, -1.5, 0], [4, -1.5, 0], color=BLUE, stroke_width=10)
hit = np.array([0, -1.5, 0])
normal = DashedLine(hit, hit + 3.2 * UP, color=GREY_B)
src = hit + 3.0 * np.array([-np.sin(40 * DEGREES), np.cos(40 * DEGREES), 0])
ray_in = Arrow(src, hit, buff=0, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(mirror), Create(normal), GrowArrow(ray_in))
stage.add(mirror, normal, ray_in)

beats.intent: The reflected ray leaving on the other side at the same 40° to the normal, both angles marked
beats.narration: It bounces off at the same angle to the normal on the other side: forty degrees in, forty degrees out.
beats.code:
out = hit + 3.0 * np.array([np.sin(40 * DEGREES), np.cos(40 * DEGREES), 0])
ray_out = Arrow(hit, out, buff=0, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(GrowArrow(ray_out))
stage.add(ray_out)
a1 = Angle(Line(hit, hit + UP), Line(hit, src), radius=0.8, color=GREEN)
a2 = Angle(Line(hit, out), Line(hit, hit + UP), radius=0.8, color=GREEN)
stage.play(Create(a1), Create(a2))
stage.add(a1, a2)
stage.label(a1, "40°", direction=UL, color=GREEN)
stage.label(a2, "40°", direction=UR, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The rays beside angle of incidence = angle of reflection
beats.narration: That is the law of reflection: the angle in equals the angle out.
